why.paragraph1: RATQ was created to bring Quranic software resources together in one clear and accessible place.
why.paragraph2: We help developers, researchers, and publishers discover useful work, understand how it can be used, and contribute resources that benefit the wider community.

whatIs.title: What is RATQ?
whatIs.paragraph1: RATQ is a community directory for Quranic libraries, SDKs, datasets, APIs, research tools, and other technical resources. It gives each resource a consistent place for its description, documentation, license, version, and access information.
whatIs.paragraph2Before: The platform also encourages careful publishing and review through the
whatIs.paragraph2After: , helping users evaluate accuracy, attribution, and technical quality before using a resource.

offer.title: What RATQ provides
offer.intro: The platform supports the full path from discovering a resource to publishing and maintaining one.

catalog.title: An organized resource catalog
catalog.description: Find Quranic libraries, datasets, APIs, SDKs, and research tools through a consistent and searchable directory.

verification.title: Clear quality information
verification.description: Review documentation, licenses, versions, attribution, and Itqan verification information before choosing a resource.

access.title: Access management for publishers
access.description: Publishers can manage restricted resources, review access requests, and keep resource information up to date.

community.title: Community feedback
community.description: Comments, reports, and reviews help identify useful resources, outdated information, and areas that need improvement.

tools.title: Tools for developers
tools.description: Developer-focused pages, API keys, documentation links, and integration details make resources easier to use in real projects.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.description: To make trusted Quranic technical resources easier to discover, understand, publish, and maintain, while supporting responsible collaboration between developers, researchers, and publishers.

vision.title: Our vision
vision.description: A connected Quranic technology community where valuable work is visible, well documented, properly attributed, and easier to build upon.

contributors.subtitle: RATQ is built with the community. These contributors have fixed bugs, closed issues, and shipped improvements to the platform.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.intro: We'd love to hear from you — a question about a resource, a suggestion to improve the platform, a bug report, or an interest in contributing code.
contact.noTeam: RATQ is a community-run open-source project — there's no separate team reviewing your contribution from the outside. Everyone working on RATQ starts from the same open queue on GitHub.
contact.issues: For technical issues, bugs, or feature requests, open a GitHub Issue
contact.forum: For general community discussion about RATQ or other Itqan projects
contact.contribute: Want to contribute code? See CONTRIBUTING.md in the repo to get started.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what data RATQ collects and why.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.item1: When you sign in as a developer via GitHub, we receive your verified email and display name from GitHub to create your account and link your session.
collect.item2: When you publish a resource or request access to one, we store the data you enter specifically for that purpose (resource description, GitHub URL, license info, and similar).
collect.item3: Your signed-in session is stored in your browser’s local storage, not a cookie. We use one short-lived cookie during GitHub sign-in itself, not for tracking.

dontDo.title: What we don't do
dontDo.item1: We don't use third-party analytics or advertising trackers on the site.
dontDo.item2: We don't sell your data or share it with outside parties for marketing purposes.

deletion.title: Requesting account or data deletion
deletion.body: Reach out via GitHub Issues (see the Contact page) and we'll handle the request.

privacy.betaNote: This is an initial policy for a platform still in Beta, and may be updated as the platform evolves.

standards.title: Itqan Standards
standards.intro: RATQ encourages careful publishing and review through the Itqan Standards, to help you evaluate any resource before using it in your project. These standards look at three things:

accuracy.title: Accuracy
accuracy.body: Is the Quranic content (text, recitation, tafsir, or related data) sourced and consistent with what it's attributed to?

completeness.title: Completeness
completeness.body: How complete and correct is the information shown about the resource — license, documentation, version, and access details?

quality.title: Technical quality
quality.body: Is the resource actively maintained, clearly documented for developers, and easy to integrate into a real project?

standards.closing: Every resource on the platform surfaces this information clearly — license, documentation, version, and access status — so you can evaluate it yourself before using it. The Itqan Standards aren't a stamp of approval from an internal team; they're a shared framework that helps the whole community evaluate resources the same way.

docs.title: Docs

browse.title: Browsing resources
browse.body: Use the resource catalog to search and filter by type, license, or keyword. Every resource page shows documentation, license, version, and access information.

publish.title: Publishing and access
publish.body: Have a resource to add? Sign in via GitHub from the developer dashboard to publish it and manage access requests if it's restricted.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.body: From the developer dashboard you can generate API keys to integrate RATQ's data directly into your project.

contribute.title: Contributing code
contribute.body: RATQ is open source. See CONTRIBUTING.md in the GitHub repo for how to set up a dev environment and contribute code.
